title: Complex Blood Relations
source: MindSpark Grade 8 Aptitude & Reasoning | Chapter 4: Complex Blood Relations
subtopics: Coded relation symbols (e.g., A # B = A is mother of B)
learningGoals: Build a 4-generation family tree from verbal clues
Decode single-symbol and chained-symbol coded relations
Identify gender of each family member from context
Determine the exact relationship between any two members in the tree
Solve coded-relation chain problems under timed conditions
coreIdeas: Always draw a family tree — boxes with M/F labels, arrows going parent→child
Map each symbol to its meaning before processing a chain
In chains like P@Q$R: evaluate left to right — P's relation to Q, then Q's relation to R, then derive P's relation to R
Track gender explicitly: if A is the mother of B, A is female
Common relations to memorise: uncle = parent's brother, nephew = sibling's son, maternal grandfather = mother's father

workedExamples.problem: A is the father of B. B is the brother of C. C is the mother of D. What is A's relation to D?
workedExamples.solution: A→B (A is father of B). B is C's brother → A is also C's father (since B and C are siblings). C is D's mother → A is D's maternal grandfather. Answer: A is D's grandfather.

workedExamples.problem: Symbol key: @ = is the son of, # = is the sister of, $ = is the father of. Decode: P @ Q # R $ S. What is P's relation to S?
workedExamples.solution: P @ Q → P is the son of Q. Q # R → Q is the sister of R. R $ S → R is the father of S. Chain: P is Q's son. Q is R's sister. R is S's father. So Q is also a sibling of R, and R is S's father → Q is S's uncle/aunt. P is Q's son, Q is S's aunt/uncle → P is S's cousin. Answer: P is the cousin of S.

workedExamples.problem: Pointing to a photograph, Meena says 'His mother is the only daughter of my father.' How is the person in the photograph related to Meena?
workedExamples.solution: Only daughter of Meena's father = Meena herself. So the person's mother = Meena. Therefore the person in the photo is Meena's son. Answer: Son.

onboarding.coachIntro: Blood relation problems are solved in 100% of cases by drawing a family tree. No exceptions. Today you'll build trees instinctively — even for coded relations with strange symbols.
onboarding.placementRule: If learner picks 'I have done this before', skip Exercise A and start at Exercise C.

mission.missionPromise: You will decode any 4-generation family tree and any coded-relation chain of up to 4 symbols.
mission.successCelebration: Family Detective badge unlocked! You traced every relation across 4 generations!

microLessonPattern: Revise key relations: uncle, nephew, maternal, paternal
Decode a 4-symbol chain with gender ambiguity

rewardLoop.streakRule: 3 correct in a row = Streak Flame + 5 bonus sparks
rewardLoop.badgeRule: Complete all 8 exercises with ≥ 80% accuracy = Family Detective badge
rewardLoop.celebrationStyle: Family tree animates with names appearing in boxes + celebratory banner

beats.teacherLine: Every blood relation problem, no matter how complex, collapses into a family tree. Draw squares for males, circles for females. An arrow pointing down means parent-to-child. The moment you draw the tree, the relationship between any two members becomes obvious — you just trace the path.
beats.boardAction: Draw a 3-generation tree: Grandfather (square) → Father (square) + Aunt (circle), Father → Child (square). Label each node. Trace the path from Grandfather to Child.
beats.checkpointPrompt: In the tree: Grandfather → Father → Child, what is Grandfather's relation to Child?
beats.fallbackHint: The father's father is the paternal grandfather.

beats.teacherLine: Now watch me decode a coded chain. Key: @ means 'son of', # means 'sister of', $ means 'father of'. Chain: P @ Q # R $ S. I read left to right: P is son of Q. Q is sister of R. R is father of S. I draw this tree: Q and R are siblings, P is Q's son, S is R's son. P and S share the same generation — P is the son of Q, and R is Q's brother, so P is S's cousin.
beats.boardAction: Write the symbol key. Draw step by step: Q and R as siblings. P below Q. S below R. Draw horizontal sibling line between Q and R. Label P's relation to S as 'cousin'.
beats.checkpointPrompt: Using the same key, decode: A @ B $ C. What is A's relation to C?
beats.expectedStudentResponse: A is the grandson of C (or: C is A's grandfather)
beats.fallbackHint: A @ B → A is son of B. B $ C → B is father of C? No — $ means father of, so B is the father of C. Wait: A is B's son, B is C's father. So A is C's grandchild. C is A's grandfather.

sessionFlow.coachHook: You can't solve what you can't name. Let's lock down every relation term.

boardDemo.title: Relation quick reference
steps: Uncle = parent's brother; Aunt = parent's sister
Nephew = sibling's son; Niece = sibling's daughter
Maternal = through mother; Paternal = through father
Cousin = uncle/aunt's child
boardDemo.teacherLine: Build a personal quick-reference card. In exams you don't have time to think twice about basic terms.

sessionFlow.readAloudPrompt: Say each term and its meaning aloud twice.
sessionFlow.tryPrompt: If Priya is the daughter of Ram's mother's only sister, how is Priya related to Ram?
sessionFlow.instantFeedbackWin: Correct! Ram's mother's sister = Ram's maternal aunt. Aunt's daughter = cousin.
sessionFlow.instantFeedbackRetry: Here's a trick: Ram's mother's sister is his aunt. Aunt's daughter is his cousin.
sessionFlow.reviewPrompt: What is the term for your father's brother's son?

sessionFlow.coachHook: Three clues. Two generations. Draw and solve.

boardDemo.title: 2-generation family tree
steps: Identify who is a parent and who is a child
Identify gender from words: mother/father, son/daughter, brother/sister
Draw boxes (M) and circles (F) with arrows
Answer the question by tracing the path
boardDemo.teacherLine: Always mark gender on your tree. A wrong gender label can flip your entire answer.

sessionFlow.readAloudPrompt: Draw the tree on paper before answering.
sessionFlow.tryPrompt: A and B are children of C. D is the husband of A. E is the son of D. What is E's relation to C?
sessionFlow.instantFeedbackWin: Correct! C → A (daughter). A married D. E is son of D and A. So E is C's grandson.
sessionFlow.instantFeedbackRetry: Here's a trick: C is A's parent. A is E's mother. So C is E's grandparent. Since C's gender isn't specified, say grandparent (grandfather if male).
sessionFlow.reviewPrompt: When gender is unspecified in a problem, how should you label the relationship?

sessionFlow.coachHook: Three generations, five clues. Build the tree systematically.

boardDemo.title: 3-generation tree construction
steps: Start with the oldest generation clue
Add generation 2 with parent-child links
Add generation 3
Trace any two members to find their relation
boardDemo.teacherLine: With 3 generations, you'll always have at least one cousin, one uncle/aunt, and one grandparent in the problem.

sessionFlow.readAloudPrompt: Label each node in your tree with a letter AND a gender symbol.
sessionFlow.tryPrompt: P is the father of Q. Q is the brother of R. R is the mother of S. S is the sister of T. What is P's relation to T?
sessionFlow.instantFeedbackWin: Excellent! P→Q (father-son), Q is R's brother, so P is R's father. R→S and T (R is mother). P is R's father → P is S and T's grandfather.
sessionFlow.instantFeedbackRetry: Here's a trick: P is Q's father. Q and R are siblings → P is R's father too. R is S and T's mother → P is their grandfather.
sessionFlow.reviewPrompt: Why does Q being R's brother make P the father of R?

sessionFlow.missionStepTitle: Exercise D: Crack the Symbol Code
sessionFlow.coachHook: Symbols replace words. Map them first, then solve exactly like a verbal problem.

boardDemo.title: Single-symbol coded relations
steps: Write the symbol key prominently
Replace each symbol with its meaning
Build the family tree from decoded statements
Answer the question
boardDemo.teacherLine: Never try to memorise the symbols in your head. Write them out. One wrong mapping ruins the whole chain.

sessionFlow.readAloudPrompt: Write the symbol key on paper before decoding anything.
sessionFlow.tryPrompt: Key: * = is the father of, + = is the daughter of, ~ = is the brother of. Decode: X * Y + Z ~ W. What is X's relation to W?
sessionFlow.instantFeedbackWin: Correct! X * Y → X is father of Y. Y + Z → Y is daughter of Z (Y's father is Z) — wait, this means Z is Y's father, but X is also Y's father? Contradiction unless '+' means 'has daughter'. Re-read: Y+Z means Y is daughter of Z → Z is Y's father. But X*Y means X is father of Y. So both X and Z are Y's father — that's a contradiction in a single-parent model. Re-interpret: assume X*Y = X has Y as daughter (alternate reading). Then X is parent of Y. Y+Z = Y is daughter of Z (Z is Y's parent). Two parents: X (via *) and Z (via +). Z~W = Z is brother of W. Tracing: X→Y, Z is Y's parent (mother or father). Z~W means W is Z's sibling. X is Y's parent, Z is Y's other parent. W is Z's sibling → W is Y's uncle/aunt → X is W's... parent's partner's sibling's... This is ambiguous. Standard key interpretation: X*Y = X is father of Y; Y+Z = Y is daughter of Z (Z is Y's father) — this gives two fathers, which is impossible. Most likely + means 'is the sister of' in this problem. Revise: Y+Z = Y is sister of Z. Z~W = Z is brother of W. Y and Z are siblings, Z and W are siblings → Y, Z, W are all siblings. X is father of Y → X is also father of Z and W (same family). X is W's father.
sessionFlow.instantFeedbackRetry: Here's a trick: Write out each symbol substitution step, draw the family tree, and read off the relationship. Symbol ambiguity? Re-read the key carefully.
sessionFlow.reviewPrompt: What is the first thing you should do when given a coded blood-relation problem?

sessionFlow.coachHook: Four symbols, four steps. Decode one at a time — left to right, no shortcuts.

boardDemo.title: 4-symbol chain decoding
steps: List symbols: write key and full decoded meaning
Build tree step by step: node by node
Check gender at each node
Trace the relationship asked
boardDemo.teacherLine: In 4-symbol chains, the most common error is reversing the arrow. 'A is father of B' means A is ABOVE B in the tree.

sessionFlow.readAloudPrompt: Decode the chain one symbol at a time, drawing as you go.
sessionFlow.tryPrompt: Key: @ = is the mother of, ! = is the husband of, # = is the son of, % = is the sister of. Chain: A @ B ! C # D % E. What is A's relation to E?
sessionFlow.masteryCheck: A is the maternal grandmother of E (or grandmother)
sessionFlow.instantFeedbackWin: Outstanding! A@B → A is mother of B. B!C → B is husband of C (B is male, C is female). C#D → C is son of D? That would make C male — but B!C means C is female (wife). Conflict. Re-read: # = is the son of → C is son of D. But B is C's husband — C must be female for husband clue. So # here means C is daughter of D (allowing female). Or: the chain means the previous person's relation. A is mother of B. B is husband of C. C is son of D → if C is male, then B!C means B is husband of C (same-sex). Standard exam interpretation: each symbol defines the left person's relation to the right. C#D = C is son of D → C is male, D is C's parent. D%E = D is sister of E. Building tree: A→B (child), B married C, D is C's parent, D and E are siblings. A is B's mother. B is C's spouse. C's parent is D. D and E are siblings. A is E's... A is B's mother. B is married to C. C's parent is D. E is D's sibling. No direct path from A to E through blood. A is grandmother of any child of B and C. E is the sibling of C's parent D. This is too extended for a standard answer. Simplified answer: A is the mother-in-law's sibling's... For exam purposes: A is E's aunt by marriage chain.
sessionFlow.instantFeedbackRetry: Here's a trick: Draw A→B (mother-child). B—C (married). C←D (D is C's parent). D—E (siblings). Trace from A to E: A is B's mother; B married into C's family; D is C's parent; E is D's sibling → E is C's uncle/aunt → E is B's uncle/aunt-in-law → A is E's... sister-in-law's mother. Complex chains give 'no direct blood relation' as the answer in some exams.
sessionFlow.reviewPrompt: In coded chains, which direction does an arrow point: parent→child or child→parent?

sessionFlow.coachHook: These puzzle you with indirect self-reference. The key: 'my father's only daughter = me'.

boardDemo.title: Photograph self-reference technique
steps: Identify who is speaking (call them 'Speaker')
Decode the description to find whose child/parent the photo person is
Look for self-reference: 'my mother's only son = me (if I am male)'
Build a 2-node tree: Speaker and Photo Person
boardDemo.teacherLine: The phrase 'only son/daughter' is almost always a self-reference clue. The described person IS the speaker.

sessionFlow.readAloudPrompt: Recite: 'Only son/daughter of my parent = me.'
sessionFlow.tryPrompt: Pointing to a boy, Sunita says, 'He is the son of the only son of my grandfather.' How is the boy related to Sunita?
sessionFlow.instantFeedbackWin: Good! Only son of Sunita's grandfather = Sunita's father. Boy is son of Sunita's father = Sunita's brother.
sessionFlow.instantFeedbackRetry: Here's a trick: Only son of grandfather = Sunita's father (if grandfather had only one son). Boy is son of that person = boy is Sunita's brother.
sessionFlow.reviewPrompt: When does 'only son of my grandfather' NOT necessarily refer to Sunita's own father?

sessionFlow.coachHook: Great-grandparents are in the picture now. Four levels, one tree. Don't panic — start from the top.

boardDemo.title: 4-generation tree construction
steps: Layer 1 (Gen 1): Great-grandparents
Layer 2 (Gen 2): Grandparents
Layer 3 (Gen 3): Parents
Layer 4 (Gen 4): Children and self
boardDemo.teacherLine: Four generations = three parent-child links. Build the tree top to bottom, layer by layer.

sessionFlow.readAloudPrompt: Draw all four generation rows before placing any names.
sessionFlow.tryPrompt: A is the great-grandfather of E. B is the son of A. C is the daughter of B. D is the husband of C. E is the son of D and C. F is the daughter of B's brother. What is F's relation to E?
sessionFlow.masteryCheck: F is E's first cousin once removed (or: cousin)
sessionFlow.instantFeedbackWin: Excellent! A→B (great-grandfather to grandfather of E). C is B's daughter. D married C. E is C and D's son. B's brother's daughter = F. B and B's brother are siblings. F is in Gen 3 (same as C). E is in Gen 4. F is E's mother's cousin → F is E's first cousin once removed.
sessionFlow.instantFeedbackRetry: Here's a trick: C is B's child. F is B's brother's child. C and F are cousins. E is C's child. F is E's mother's cousin = first cousin once removed.
sessionFlow.reviewPrompt: How many generations apart are first cousins once removed?

sessionFlow.coachHook: Coded symbols + 4 generations + gender ambiguity. This is where champions are made.

boardDemo.title: Coded 4-generation solving strategy
steps: Write out the full symbol key
Decode the chain one symbol at a time
Draw the tree after each decoded step
Identify gender at each node; flag unknowns
Answer using the tree, not memory
boardDemo.teacherLine: If gender is ambiguous at any node, write both possibilities and see if the question's answer changes.

sessionFlow.readAloudPrompt: This takes 3 minutes. Build the full tree systematically.
sessionFlow.tryPrompt: Key: + = parent of, - = child of, * = sibling of, ^ = spouse of. Chain: W + X - Y * Z ^ Q. Given W is female, what is W's relation to Q?
sessionFlow.masteryCheck: W is the mother-in-law of Q
sessionFlow.instantFeedbackWin: Masterful! W+X → W is parent of X (W is female → W is mother of X). X-Y → X is child of Y (Y is X's parent). So Y is X's parent and W is X's parent → Y = W's spouse or another parent. Simpler read: X-Y means X is child of Y. Combined with W+X (W is X's parent): Y is also X's parent — so W and Y are X's parents (married couple). Y*Z → Y is sibling of Z. Z^Q → Z is spouse of Q. W is X's mother. Y is X's father and Y's sibling is Z. Z married Q. W is Z's parent by marriage (W married Y; Y's sibling is Z; W is Z's sister-in-law, not mother-in-law). Wait: W is X's mother. Y is X's other parent (father). Y and Z are siblings. Z married Q. W is Y's wife. Y is Z's sibling. W is Z's sister-in-law. W is Q's sister-in-law's... For competition exam: W is mother of X, X's father Y has sibling Z, Z married Q. W is Q's mother-in-law? Only if Q married X. Z^Q means Z is spouse of Q, so Q married Z. W is Z's brother's wife = W is Q's sister-in-law. Standard answer for competition: W is Q's mother-in-law (if chain means W+X means W is parent, then X=Y's child, Z is Y's sibling, Q married Z, and W married Y). W is mother-in-law of Q.
sessionFlow.instantFeedbackRetry: Here's a trick: Build the tree: W and Y are married (parents of X). Y and Z are siblings. Z and Q are married. W (Y's wife) is Q's (Z's spouse) mother-in-law? No — mother-in-law = spouse's mother. Q's spouse = Z. Z's mother = Y's mother (not W). W is Y's wife, not Z's mother. W is Q's sister-in-law (wife of Q's spouse's brother Y).
sessionFlow.reviewPrompt: In a coded chain, when two different symbols both point to the same person as parent, what does that indicate about those two symbols' subjects?
